title: Patience
definition: Patience is Spirit-formed endurance, restraint, and trust while waiting on God and bearing with others in love.
summary: Patience is Spirit-formed endurance and restraint under delay, difficulty, weakness, provocation, or suffering.
christFocus: Jesus Christ patiently endures with His people and teaches them to wait, forgive, and persevere.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on faithful waiting and long-suffering love. Patience trusts God's timing, bears with people, resists retaliation, and continues obedience when change is slow. It reflects the patience God has shown toward sinners.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because impatience often reveals unbelief, control, or lack of love. Patience protects relationships and helps believers endure sanctification as a long work of grace. It also makes the Church safer for weak and growing people.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Notice where delay or irritation exposes your heart. Slow down your reactions and pray before responding. Remember how patiently the Lord has dealt with you.
